subject: Renewal & scale: smoothing proposal and voucher option
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martin <alex@brightgrid.com>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 6 Sep 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal & scale: pricing options to cover mid‑term growth

Alex —

Thanks again for the candid conversation last week. Per our call, I pulled together three pragmatic paths so BrightGrid can cover the expected 30% mid‑term growth next year while keeping near‑term economics predictable. See the attached Pricing_Workbook.xlsx for the line‑by‑line numbers, but high level options are below: 

1) Standard renewal + uplift (fastest)
   - 12‑month renewal at current committed capacity + 10% uplift to cover projected token growth
   - Standard SLA and access to burst capacity
   - Invoice on renewal date

2) Phased smoothing + voucher credits (recommended for predictability)
   - 6% immediate uplift at renewal + a 9‑month voucher ladder worth 4% of current commit applied monthly as consumption credits (auto‑apply)
   - Vouchers usable against overage or additional model classes; non‑refundable but transferable across sub‑accounts
   - Net effective uplift over 12 months ≈ 8% if utilization follows forecast

3) Top‑up + co‑term (min admin friction)
   - One‑time top‑up purchase that increases committed capacity immediately; co‑term aligns with existing contract expiry and amortizes price
   - Flexible conversion to on‑demand at month 10 if growth slows

Ask: Which of these aligns best with procurement constraints? If you want, we can draft a short SOW amendment and a co‑term schedule.

I know pricing is sensitive — Marissa is on the thread for any escalation and to confirm discount authority. If helpful, we can also offer a one‑time bridge credit to smooth the first billing period while vouchers ramp.

Attachments: Pricing_Workbook.xlsx (summary and model)

Cheers,
Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555‑0192

From: Alex Martin <alex@brightgrid.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@brightgrid.com, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 6 Sep 2026 12:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal & scale: pricing options to cover mid‑term growth

Ben —

Thanks for the clear options and workbook. A few quick notes from our side after an internal review: 

- 10% uplift up front is a hard pill for our finance team given existing forecasts.
- The voucher ladder sounds interesting, but procurement will want the vouchers to cover overages first (not limit to model classes).
- Co‑term/top‑up is attractive if we can avoid a big one‑time hit on the P&L in Q4.

Procurement (cc) asked if you can: 
  • reduce the immediate uplift to 5% and make the voucher ladder worth 6% over 9 months, OR
  • provide a 3‑month bridge credit to offset the first billing cycle while we ramp usage into the new commit.

Can you confirm what pieces are flexible versus firm? Also, we prefer a short SOW amendment with an explicit credit application example so our finance team can model it.

Thanks — I’ll get procurement to share any contract routing requirements if we move forward.

Best,
Alex Martin
Director of Platform, BrightGrid
alex@brightgrid.com

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: Renewal & scale: pricing options to cover mid‑term growth — internal decision notes

Ben / Marissa —

Dropping a quick internal note so we have alignment before we respond to Alex/procurement. Key constraints Alex highlighted: finance wants lower up‑front delta, procurement wants vouchers to apply to overages, and they prefer smoothing vs. one big top‑up.

I think we can accommodate with a combined approach:

• Offer A (preferred for BrightGrid): 5% immediate uplift + 9‑month voucher ladder worth 6% of current commit applied as overage credits. Vouchers auto‑apply to overage line items.

• Bridge credit: 3‑month fee credit equivalent to their estimated first‑month overage (capped at $25k) to offset the P&L bump. This is one‑time and contingent on signing the SOW amendment within 14 days.

• Internal tradeoffs: effective uplift over 12 months ~6.5% (if utilization follows forecast). We should position this as helping them smooth cash flow while protecting Redwood against sustained higher usage above forecast.

Marissa — do you approve the bridge cap and voucher transferability? If you prefer, I can frame it as a conditional credit (sign + 30‑day invoice hold) instead of cash credit.

If approved, I’ll ask Ben to send a clean SOW amendment and DocuSign envelope and attach BrightGrid_SOW_v2.pdf with the voucher ladder table.

— Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
AM, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai

Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2026 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Final proposal: 5% uplift + voucher ladder + 3‑month bridge credit (SOW & DocuSign)

Alex / procurement team —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Per our internal alignment, please see the revised terms below and the attached SOW amendment (BrightGrid_SOW_v2.pdf):

Summary of agreed commercial terms (for SOW amendment):
• Term: 12‑month renewal starting Oct 1, 2026
• Immediate uplift: 5% increase to committed capacity at renewal
• Voucher ladder: total vouchers equal to 6% of current annual commit, applied monthly over 9 months as automatic credits that first offset overage usage; vouchers transferable across BrightGrid sub‑accounts
• Bridge credit: one‑time credit applied to first post‑renewal invoice equal to actual billed overage up to $25,000 (contingent on SOW signed within 14 days)

I’ve opened a DocuSign envelope for the SOW amendment and statement table: https://www.docusign.com/sign/abcdef123456 — the SOW includes a worked example of invoice math to make it simple for your finance team. Once signed we’ll schedule the contract amendment and confirm the voucher activation schedule.

If procurement needs any specific invoice wording for capitalization, let me know and we’ll include it in the SOW.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this quickly.

Best,
Ben
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
